title: Implement PipeWire registry and object lifetime engine
description:
Create PipeWireContext, the event-driven PipeWire registry listener that tracks global objects (nodes, ports, links) through their full lifecycle.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

Before editing, inspect:
- PipeWire 0.3 API headers: spa/utils/hook.h, pipewire/core.h, pipewire/registry.h, pipewire/proxy.h
- Any existing src/pipewire/ files for project conventions
- CMakeLists.txt for existing PipeWire link targets

Do not infer APIs, schemas, behavior, or file contents; inspect the referenced files first.

Implementation:
1. PipeWireContext.hpp — declare PipeWireContext class owning a pw_main_loop (or pw_thread_loop), pw_context, pw_core, and pw_registry. Expose lifecycle methods: start(), stop(), isRunning(). Define a nested GlobalObject struct holding uint32_t id, const char* type, uint32_t version, pw_proxy*, and spa_hook listener. Declare signal-style callbacks (std::function or Qt signal) for globalAdded(uint32_t id, const char* type, const spa_dict* props) and globalRemoved(uint32_t id). Declare a std::unordered_map<uint32_t, GlobalObject> for tracked objects.
2. PipeWireContext.cpp — implement pw_registry_events with .global and .global_remove handlers. In the global handler, create a pw_proxy via pw_registry_bind, store the GlobalObject, and invoke globalAdded. In global_remove, destroy the proxy, erase the object, and invoke globalRemoved. Use pw_thread_loop for thread safety: lock/unlock around map mutations. start() creates the PipeWire objects and starts the thread loop; stop() quits the loop, destroys proxies, and tears down in reverse order. Handle pw_core error and done events for connection-loss detection.

Constraints:
- Do NOT shell out to pw-dump, pw-cli, or wpctl.
- Do NOT perform file I/O, allocation-heavy work, or blocking calls inside PipeWire callbacks.
- Use C++20 features where appropriate (structured bindings, std::format, concepts).
- All PipeWire proxy and hook listener lifetimes must be explicitly managed; prevent use-after-free on rapid add/remove cycles.
acceptance_criteria: src/pipewire/PipeWireContext.hpp exists and declares PipeWireContext with start(), stop(), isRunning(), globalAdded/globalRemoved callbacks, and a GlobalObject map
src/pipewire/PipeWireContext.cpp implements pw_registry_events .global and .global_remove handlers that bind proxies and track object lifetime
PipeWireContext uses pw_thread_loop for thread-safe registry access, not pw_main_loop on the calling thread
No calls to popen, system(), QProcess, pw-dump, pw-cli, or wpctl appear in either file
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only -I/usr/include/pipewire-0.3 -I/usr/include/spa-0.2 src/pipewire/PipeWireContext.hpp succeeds or the file is parseable as valid C++20 with PipeWire headers
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: add new third-party dependencies beyond PipeWire 0.3 and standard library
create shell-out or subprocess calls to PipeWire CLI tools

allowed: choose pw_thread_loop vs pw_main_loop for thread model
choose std::function callbacks vs Qt signals for notification
choose RAII wrapper vs explicit destroy for proxy lifetime
forbidden: introduce a plugin or extension framework
add PipeWire filter or stream objects in this task
